name: Repeat

x.description: Input tensor, any shape (1D-4D). Supports float32, float16, bfloat16.

repeats.description: list of ints, number of repeats per dimension (e.g. [2, 1, 2]).

y.description: Repeated tensor, same dtype as x, each dim multiplied by repeats.

description:
Repeat: Repeats a tensor along the specified dimensions.

torch.Tensor.repeat = repeat(*repeats) -> Tensor

Repeats this tensor along the specified dimensions. Unlike expand(), this function copies the tensor's data.

Tensor.repeat behaves differently from numpy.repeat but is more similar to numpy.tile. For the operator similar to numpy.repeat, see torch.repeat_interleave.

Args:
    repeats (torch.Size, int..., tuple of int or list of int): The number of times to repeat this tensor along each dimension.

Example:
    >>> x = torch.tensor([1, 2, 3])
    >>> x.repeat(4, 2)
    tensor([[1, 2, 3, 1, 2, 3],
            [1, 2, 3, 1, 2, 3],
            [1, 2, 3, 1, 2, 3],
            [1, 2, 3, 1, 2, 3]])
    >>> x.repeat(4, 2, 1).size()
    torch.Size([4, 2, 3])

Returns: Tensor, same dtype, shape = x.shape * repeats.
